pr_title: drivers: nrf_qspi_nor: Add support for S2B1 QER modes
pr_body:
Add support for S2B1v4 quad-enable-requirements. Tested with Winbond
W25Q128JV series and pp4o and read4io commands.

Fixes #42333.

Signed-off-by: Zack Cornelius <zcornelius@securityesys.com>

@carlescufi I am going to check this out, and build this for my board now, but looking at the code something seems wrong. At least for the GD25 chip on the Adafruit board. According to that manual, to write to the registers the chip uses 01H opcode, and expects 2 bytes following, one for status register 1 and register2. While it is possible it supports the alternative opcode (31H), this is not documented.
page 13 [here](https://cdn-shop.adafruit.com/product-files/4763/4763_GD25Q16CTIGR.pdf)

However, it does seem that this branch *DOES* work, so it seems like the chip does support the opcode, I am able to use the flash chip with; writetoc=pp40, readoc=read4o, quad-enable-requirements="S2B1v6".

It seems like I could have saved myself A LOT of time had I tried this all out just a bit later instead of last week. I would not have needed to pour over manuals about nor chips and qspi, but I guess learning about new stuff is always worth while. Thanks for having this patch ready, I will go close my pr.
If it is possible, can you update the Adafruit nrf52840 dev tree to use these values on this pull request?
@natelust I updated the adafruit feather nrf52840 dts to use quad mode by default - Can you test with this updated branch and make sure I didn't break anything on that?

Unfortunately, I will not be back to my computer for a while, I will test when I am though, but I guess don't let me hold you up. Looking over this, the only difference from what my DT was is that I used S2B1v6, but looking at your code path, it should not make any difference. Thanks for adding that.
There does seem to be a weird white space issue going on though, but I cant be sure that is not just github rendering.

I feel like I should chime in here. Here is the documentation regarding QER [JEDEC](https://www.jedec.org/standards-documents/docs/jesd216b)(Page 40, or search `QER`):
```
This field describes whether the device contains a Quad Enable (QE) bit used to enable 1S-1S-4S and 1S-4S-4S
quad read or quad program operations. If QE exists, this field also identifies the bit location and method to set/clear
the bit.
In this standard, status register 1 refers to the first data byte transferred on a Read Status (05h) or Write Status (01h)
command. Status register 2 refers to the byte read using instruction 35h. Status register 2 is the second byte
transferred in a Write Status (01h) command. Bits are numbered from 7 to 0, where bit 7 is transferred first on the
wire.
NOTE Industry naming and definitions of these status registers may differ. The user will typically perform a readmodify-write sequence of operations to maintain the state of all other writable status register bits. For example read
both status registers, set/clear QE, Write Status with both data bytes

000b: Device does not have a QE bit. Device detects 1S-1S-4S and 1S-4S-4S reads based on instruction.
IO3/HOLD# functions as hold during instruction phase

001b: QE is bit 1 of status register 2. It is set via Write Status with two data bytes where bit 1 of the second
byte is one. It is cleared via Write Status with two data bytes where bit 1 of the second byte is zero.
Writing only one byte to the status register has the side-effect of clearing status register 2, including the
QE bit. The 100b code is used if writing one byte to the status register does not modify status register 2.

010b: QE is bit 6 of status register 1. It is set via Write Status with one data byte where bit 6 is one. It is cleared
via Write Status with one data byte where bit 6 is zero.

011b: QE is bit 7 of status register 2. It is set via Write status register 2 instruction 3Eh with one data byte
where bit 7 is one. It is cleared via Write status register 2 instruction 3Eh with one data byte where bit 7
is zero. The status register 2 is read using instruction 3Fh.

100b: QE is bit 1 of status register 2. It is set via Write Status with two data bytes where bit 1 of the second
byte is one. It is cleared via Write Status with two data bytes where bit 1 of the second byte is zero. In
contrast to the 001b code, writing one byte to the status register does not modify status register 2.

101b: QE is bit 1 of the status register 2. Status register 1 is read using Read Status instruction 05h. Status
register 2 is read using instruction 35h. QE is set via Write Status instruction 01h with two data bytes
where bit 1 of the second byte is one. It is cleared via Write Status with two data bytes where bit 1 of the
second byte is zero.

110b: QE is bit 1 of the status register 2. Status register 1 is read using Read Status instruction 05h. Status
register 2 is read using instruction 35h, and status register 3 is read using instruction 15h. QE is set via
Write Status Register instruction 31h with one data byte where b
```

Given what I've read, I do not think S2B1V4 is the correct mode for a W25Q128JV since the Read SR1 Command (01h) only returns SR1. Though, as far as I can tell, what you've implemented is S2B1v6 which is what this chip wants anyway.

@natelust I'm a little bit confused about how the branch managed to work for your chip which appears to use S2B1v5. Also, this doesn't appear to be consistent in the chip family since the gd25q16e is S2B1v5, but the gd25q128e I'm using is S2B1v6.

P.S. Sorry for going AWOL on my branch/pull-request. I didn't notice it had gotten comments on it after it had gone stale.

EDIT: After reviewing more code and documentation, I have come to the conclusion that I am confused. I've replaced my summaries with the full text of the documentation. (Which is copied verbatim into linux source code, so there shouldn't be a problem posting it here.) There is also a spi-nor driver that might be worth referencing.
https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/sfdp.c
https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/sfdp.h
https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/core.c

@legoabram @zackcornelius My guess is this board for whatever reason had the quad enable bit set before I even opened it. I forced the bit to 0, verified reads and writes were not working, and tested this patch completely fresh. This patch **does not** make the adafruit board work.

However, I think it is possible to incorporate some of the changes from my branch into this branch (using the existing JDEEC flag) to enable support for the AF board. I will have a go at this, but if you get to it before I do feel free to grab whatever from my closed PR you want.

I modified the code to work with my board and put a pull request to @zackcornelius branch, he can pull that in and it should show up here. Otherwise I can make a new PR, but this seemed easier to keep track of things.

@natelust The only differences between the behavior of v1 and v5 are when writing sr1, v1 also writes sr2  (as the sr2 values will be cleared by writing), while v5 writes just sr1. The code path for writing sr2 stays the same between the 2. 

v1 and v5 are functionally identical right now though, since the only time we write to the status registers at all is just when setting QER (so there'd never be another write to sr1 anyway)

issue_context.title: Cannot write to qspi flash in adafruit feather nrf52840, device tree is wrong
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The qspi flash chip on the adafruit feather nrf52840 does not support the write mode supplied in the devicetree file, meaning that no writes are possible. This lead to interesting issues when trying to define a partition and use it for DFU.

Switching to SPI mode proved to be too slow, and caused out of memory issues when attempting a DFU due mcumgr getting data faster than the chip could erase. Working around that issue cause timeout errors because writes could be be completed within the hard coded 10 microsecond timeout.

Ideally one would use quad mode to interact with the chip, but as noted in a previous commit, this was not possible because the flash chip required quad mode to be enabled by setting bit 1 (second bit) in register 2. However, the nordic driver only supported enabling quad mode if the bit was 6 in register 1. While this seems to be the jedec standard (I don't have a copy of the spects to verify), this chip and possibly some others do not fully conform to this.

This leaves things in a state where it is impossible to use unless someone changes to timeout manually.

I have a pull request that I will link in the comments (chicken and egg with description of pr and issue) that addresses this by allowing a user to specify which bit corresponds to the QE bit in the device tree. It defaults to the current behavior, but the pull request also modifies the DT of the adafruit board to make the appropriate change.

Please also mention any information which could help others to understand
the problem you're facing:
 - What target platform are you using?
 I developed against the board mentioned above on zephyr 2.7 and 3.0 master. The pull request is the code against 3.0
 - What have you tried to diagnose or workaround this issue?
I sort of covered this in the description, but this involved working through the DFU subsystem to discover the problem, leading me to the flash later, then going through the driver line by line in an editor and a debugger. I was able to make things work in SPI mode, by changing time out parameters in the nordic external module, but it was too slow to be of practical use, no one will wait 10s of minuets for a firmware upgrade. I made the changes to the zephyr source code driver to enable quad mode, and have it up and running on a live board. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Load a zephyr image with a partition on the flash configured and attempt to write to it.

**Expected behavior**
I expect to be able to write to the flash chip, and use it in conjunction with the DFU firmware, in quad mode

**Impact**
show stopper, as someone cant use the external flash as is.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: (e.g. Linux, MacOS, Windows)
 Linux
 - Toolchain (e.g Zephyr SDK, ...)
 Zephyr 2.7, 3.0, sdk version 0.13.1
 - Commit SHA or Version used
Zephyr 2.7 - 8f539523b67036c4d238c3ab5e50a7a28da776b6, Zephyr 3.0 I'm not sure the exact hash, was head 2 days ago, but some merges have happened since then.

**Additional context**
A thanks to people on discord who helped point me at documentation et al on background so I could work through this issue.
comments: The pull request corresponding to this issue is: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/42334
This seems to be fixed in: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/42049. Thank you for your time looking at this issue and pull request.
It turns out the other PR does not in fact fix this issue (yet?) So I am reopening this issue to keep track of that until it does.
